examples.en: Look at those sparkly little eyes!
The baby has bright little eyes.

note: An affectionate, rhyming expression for a child's shining eyes.

key: phr:као да те је киша поквасила
meanings: you look washed out and tired
forms: literally: as if the rain had soaked you

examples.sr: Што си такав, [ка̏о да те је кѝша по̀квасила]?
examples.en: Why do you look so washed out, as if you'd been caught in the rain?

examples.sr: Изгледаш [ка̏о да те је кѝша по̀квасила].
examples.en: You look limp and worn out.
He bought a sweater of some indeterminate color.
The wall was some murky, drab color.

forms: literally: when a dead man farts

examples.en: He'll pay you when pigs fly.

examples.sr: Тај воз ће стићи [ка̏д мр̀тав пр̏дне].
examples.en: That train will arrive when hell freezes over.

note: Colloquial and a bit rude: said of something you will never see.

examples.en: Don't stop, keep going!
A little more, keep pushing to the end!

note: A shout from Balkan weddings that went viral in 2022: keep up the pace, don't give up.

key: phr:добити тањир супе и ногу у дупе
meanings: to get nothing for one's trouble
forms: literally: to get a plate of soup and a kick in the backside

examples.sr: Радио је годину дана и [до̀био та̏њир су̏пе и но̏гу у ду̏пе].
examples.en: He worked for a year and ended up with nothing.

examples.sr: Није му платила, [до̀био је та̏њир су̏пе и но̏гу у ду̏пе].
examples.en: She didn't pay him: he got nothing for his trouble.

note: Colloquial and a bit rude: to get nothing in return for your work.

examples.en: I'm going to take a half-hour nap.
After lunch he took a nap.

note: A pun: «хрчак» (hamster) and «хркати» (to snore).

examples.en: Somebody let a dove out in the elevator.

examples.sr: Тихо је [пу̏стио го̏луба] и насмејао се.
examples.en: He quietly let a dove out and laughed.
There's only odds and ends in the drawer.
I didn't buy anything, just little trinkets.

note: Colloquial and playful: small, useless things.

meanings: aren't you ugly! (said fondly to a baby)

examples.en: Aren't you ugly, my little one!

examples.sr: Бака му је рекла [што̏ си га̀дан] због урока.
examples.en: Grandma told him he was ugly, to ward off the evil eye.

note: Babies are called «гадан» or «ружан» to ward off the evil eye (урок): one does not praise them directly.

examples.en: I love you, forever yours.
He signed the letter: forever yours.

note: A man writes «заувек твој».

key: phr:не могу да престанем да читам

examples.sr: Књига је тако добра, [не мо̀гу да пре̏станем да чи̏там]!
examples.en: The book is so good, I can't stop reading!

examples.sr: Већ је поноћ, а [не мо̀гу да пре̏станем да чи̏там].
examples.en: It's already midnight, and I can't stop reading.

meanings: when does the next train leave?

examples.sr: Извините, [ка̏да по̀лази сле̏дећи во̑з] за Ниш?
examples.en: Excuse me, when does the next train to Niš leave?

examples.sr: Реците ми, [ка̏да по̀лази сле̏дећи во̑з] за Суботицу?
examples.en: Tell me, when does the next train to Subotica leave?

meanings: where can I leave my luggage?

examples.sr: Молим вас, [где̏ мо̀гу да о̏ставим пр̀тља̄г]?
examples.en: Excuse me, where can I leave my luggage?

examples.sr: Да ли знате [где̏ мо̀гу да о̏ставим пр̀тља̄г]?
examples.en: Do you know where I can leave my luggage?

key: phr:да ли је воз на време

examples.en: Is the train on time?

examples.sr: Питам [да ли је во̑з на вре́ме].
examples.en: I'm asking whether the train is on time.
Excuse me, this seat is taken.

examples.sr: Не можете да седнете, [о̀во̄ ме̏сто је резѐрвисано].
examples.en: You can't sit here, this seat is reserved.
He has no luck in love.
No luck with the lottery today.

note: In the past tense: «није имао среће» - he was unlucky.

examples.sr: Професорка нам је [по̀желела сре̏ћу] пре испита.
examples.en: The professor wished us luck before the exam.
Everyone wished him luck.
He tried his luck at gambling.

examples.sr: Хоћу да [о̏кушам сре̏ћу] у великом граду.
examples.en: I want to try my luck in a big city.

forms: literally: to be of a lucky hand

examples.sr: Он је баш [сре̏ћне ру̏ке], све му полази за руком.
examples.en: He's really lucky, everything works out for him.

examples.sr: Мој брат је [сре̏ћне ру̏ке] у послу.
examples.en: My brother is lucky in business.

meanings: to be more lucky than smart
forms: literally: to have more luck than sense

examples.sr: [И̏мала сам ви̏ше сре̏ће не̏го па̏мети]: положила сам, а нисам учила.
examples.en: I was luckier than I was smart: I passed without studying.
He's luckier than he is smart.
The doctor recommends a healthy diet.
A healthy diet gives you energy.

note: Variants: «балансирана», «уравнотежена исхрана».

examples.en: I burn calories by swimming.
I want to burn off some calories after lunch.

examples.sr: Лако је [одржа́вати здра̀ву тежѝну] уз кретање.
examples.en: It's easy to maintain a healthy weight if you stay active.
I'm trying to maintain a healthy weight.

examples.sr: Лекар ми је рекао да [огра̀ничим у̏нос ше̏ћера].
examples.en: The doctor told me to limit my sugar intake.
One should limit sugar intake.

note: Likewise: «унос соли, масти, меса».

examples.en: He decided to quit smoking.
I want to quit smoking by summer.

forms: literally: the rain pours as if from a bucket

examples.en: It's pouring outside.

examples.sr: Не излази, [кѝша ли̏је̄ ка̏о из ка̏бла]!
examples.en: Don't go out, it's pouring!

note: «Кабао» is a large bucket or tub.

meanings: I got soaked to the skin
forms: literally: I got wet to the bare skin

examples.sr: Без кишобрана [по̀кисао сам до го̀ле ко̏же].
examples.en: Without an umbrella, I got soaked to the skin.
We all got soaked to the skin.

meanings: to get caught in the rain

examples.sr: На путу кући [у̏хватила ме је кѝша].
examples.en: I got caught in the rain on the way home.

examples.sr: Узми кишобран да те не [у̏хвати кѝша].
examples.en: Take an umbrella so you don't get caught in the rain.
Around noon the sky clouded over.
Look, the sky is getting gloomy.

examples.sr: Изнад града [на̀вукли су се та̑мнӣ о̏бла̄ци].
examples.en: Dark clouds have rolled in over the city.

key: phr:и ја имам коња за трку
meanings: I've got something to compete with too
I have an ace up my sleeve too
forms: literally: I also have a horse for the race

examples.sr: Не брини, [и ја̏ ѝма̄м ко̀ња за тр̏ку].
examples.en: Don't worry, I have an ace up my sleeve too.

examples.sr: Нека се они хвале, [и ја̏ ѝма̄м ко̀ња за тр̏ку].
examples.en: Let them brag, I have an ace in the hole too.

note: Quiet confidence: said by someone who has a trump card in reserve.

key: phr:упала ми је кашика у мед
forms: literally: the spoon fell into the honey for me

examples.sr: Добио сам посао - [у̏пала ми је ка̀шика у ме̑д]!
examples.en: I got the job - I hit the jackpot!

examples.sr: Нашла је стан близу посла, [у̏пала јој је ка̀шика у ме̑д].
examples.en: She found an apartment near work - she really lucked out.

note: Said when someone has had a big stroke of luck.

meanings: were you born in a barn?
forms: literally: you were not born in a boat

examples.en: Close the door, were you born in a barn!

examples.sr: Опет су врата отворена? [Ни̏си у ча̏мцу ро̏ђен]!
examples.en: The door is open again? Were you born in a barn?

note: A reproach to someone who has left a door open.

examples.en: He came home furious.
Don't go near him, he's furious.

meanings: to be silent as a fish

examples.en: He said nothing, he's keeping mum.
Promise you'll keep quiet about it.

meanings: to sleep like a lamb (quietly and peacefully)

examples.en: The baby is sleeping like a lamb.
After a walk I sleep like a baby.

examples.sr: Он [ра̏ди ка̏о ко̏њ], а нема одмора.
examples.en: He works like a horse, and there's no rest.
Mother works like a horse for the family.
Grandpa is wise as an owl.
Ask her, she's wise as an owl.
That merchant is sly as a fox.

examples.sr: Не веруј му, [лу̏кав је ка̏о лѝсица].
examples.en: Don't trust him, he's sly as a fox.
My brother is stubborn as a mule.

examples.sr: Не слуша никога, [твр̏доглава је ка̏о ма̀гарац].
examples.en: She doesn't listen to anyone, she's stubborn as a mule.
My sister is hardworking as an ant.
He works hard, like an ant.
Today I'm slow as a snail.
Traffic is crawling like a snail.
The runner is fast as a hare.
This cat is fast as a hare.
He is loyal as a dog.
Her friend is loyal as a dog.
He's thin as a rake.

examples.sr: Откако је на дијети, [мр̏шав је ка̏о гли́ста].
examples.en: Ever since he went on a diet, he's been skinny as a rail.
The girl sings like a nightingale.
Grandma used to sing like a nightingale.
That guy is strong as an ox.
He's small, but strong as an ox.

key: phr:гледати као теле у шарена врата
forms: literally: to look like a calf at a painted door

examples.sr: Шта си се загледао, [гле̏да̄ш ка̏о тѐле у ша̏рена вра́та]?
examples.en: What are you staring at, why do you look so bewildered?

examples.sr: Гледао је [ка̏о тѐле у ша̏рена вра́та], ништа није разумео.
examples.en: He stared blankly, he didn't understand a thing.

examples.sr: - Попио сам само два пива. - [Чу̑ј] два!
examples.en: - I only had two beers. - Two, yeah right!

examples.sr: - Не можеш сам да подигнеш џак. - [Чу̑ј] не могу!
examples.en: - You can't lift the sack by yourself. - Can't, my foot!

note: Put before an echo of the other person's words, in surprise or irony; literally «listen».

examples.sr: Купио сам карту за хиљаду динара, [чу̑ј ме̏не], евра!
examples.en: I bought a ticket for a thousand dinars, what am I saying, euros!

examples.sr: Стижем у два, [чу̑ј ме̏не], у три сата.
examples.en: I'll arrive at two, I mean, at three o'clock.

note: A playful quick correction after a slip of the tongue.

forms: literally: to drive poppy seeds onto a thread

examples.sr: Немој да [те̏раш ма̏к на ко̀нац], важно је да је проблем решен.
examples.en: Don't split hairs, what matters is that the problem is solved.

examples.sr: Он увек [те̏ра ма̏к на ко̀нац] око ситница.
examples.en: He's always nitpicking over trifles.

meanings: a kum (best man, godfather) can't be replaced like a button

examples.en: The godfather isn't a button, he has to be invited.

examples.sr: Не можеш га заменити, [ку̑м нѝје ду̀гме].
examples.en: You can't replace him, a kum is not a button.

note: The «кум» (best man, godfather) is a key figure in Serbian culture.

meanings: to look for a needle in a haystack

examples.sr: Тражити га у граду је као [тра́жити и̏глу у пла̏сту се̏на].
examples.en: Looking for him in the city is like looking for a needle in a haystack.

examples.sr: Не [тра̏жи и̏глу у пла̏сту се̏на], питај некога.
examples.en: Don't look for a needle in a haystack, ask somebody.

examples.sr: Потписали смо [у̏гово̄р о за̏купу] на годину дана.
examples.en: We signed a one-year lease agreement.

examples.sr: У [у̀говору о за̏купу] стоји и депозит.
examples.en: The lease agreement also mentions the deposit.
The notary prepared the sales contract.
We're signing the sales contract on Monday.
I've been waiting for my residence permit for a month.
She renewed her residence permit.

meanings: to cling on for dear life
forms: literally: to hold on like a drunk to a fence

examples.en: He clings to his job for dear life.

examples.sr: Не [др̏жи се ка̏о пѝјан пло̏та] старих навика.
examples.en: Don't cling to old habits.

note: A drunk holds on to a fence so as not to fall: to cling stubbornly to something.

forms: literally: let everything go its own course

examples.sr: Не мешај се, [не̏ка све̏ и̏де сво̀јӣм то̑ком].
examples.en: Don't interfere, let things take their course.
Leave it, let things take their course.

note: A synonym of «само полако».

meanings: to have a sense of decency
to have a sense of honor

examples.en: He's a decent man, he will never lie.
How can you have the nerve to ask for that?

note: The negative «немати образа» means to behave shamelessly.

examples.sr: Он има [чи̏ст о̀браз], увек говори истину.
examples.en: He has a spotless reputation, he always tells the truth.

examples.sr: [Чи̏ст о̀браз] му је важнији од новца.
examples.en: His good name matters more to him than money.

forms: literally: to figure out on the ace

examples.sr: Сконтао је [на ке́ца] шта му тражим.
examples.en: He understood right away what I was asking him for.
The girl caught on to everything instantly.

note: «Кец» is a Hungarian loanword: an ace, also the grade 1.

examples.sr: Није се спремао, [и̏шао је гр̏лом у ја̏годе].
examples.en: He didn't prepare, he just rushed in headlong.

examples.sr: Не иди [гр̏лом у ја̏годе], прво размисли.
examples.en: Don't rush in headlong, think first.

meanings: to poke one's nose into other people's business

examples.sr: Немој да [гу̏раш но̑с] у туђе ствари.
examples.en: Don't poke your nose into other people's business.
The neighbor is always poking her nose into everything.

meanings: to have an eye for something

examples.en: You have an eye for this kind of work.
She has an eye for beautiful things.

meanings: at the end of the world

examples.en: He lives in the middle of nowhere.
Their house is at the end of the world.

forms: literally: it burns under my heels

examples.sr: [Го̏рӣ ми под пѐтама], рок је сутра.
examples.en: I'm under heavy pressure, the deadline is tomorrow.

examples.sr: Њему [го̏рӣ под пѐтама], а он мирује.
examples.en: He's in hot water, and yet he stays calm.

forms: literally: not even up to the knee

examples.sr: Он му [ни до ко̏лена] не стиже.
examples.en: He can't hold a candle to him.
Next to her, I can't hold a candle.

examples.sr: - Могу ли да уђем? - [Ка̏ко да не]!
examples.en: - May I come in? - Of course!

examples.sr: - Биће готово за пет минута. - [Ка̏ко да не]...
examples.en: - It'll be done in five minutes. - Yeah, right...

note: The meaning depends on tone: calm means sincere agreement, a smirk or a pause means sarcasm.

examples.sr: Ма [ма̏ни се] глупости, боље хајде на кафу.
examples.en: Oh, forget that nonsense, let's go for a coffee instead.
Drop it, it's not worth the effort.

note: «манути се» + gen.: to drop something; «мани ме се» - leave me alone.

examples.sr: Киша пада, [шта̏ да ра̏дим], остајем код куће.
examples.en: It's raining, what can I do, I'm staying home.
There's no time, what can you do.
You got the job? No way!

examples.sr: [Ма̏ не̏мој] да плачеш, све ће бити у реду.
examples.en: Oh, don't cry, everything will be fine.

note: «немој» + «да»/infinitive is a prohibition, but this reply on its own expresses surprise.

examples.en: He's late again? Don't get me started!
Prices are crazy. - Tell me about it.

note: Agreement with feeling when the other person complains or is surprised.

examples.sr: [Где̏ си], бре, одавно те нисмо видели!
examples.en: Hey, where have you been, we haven't seen you in ages!
Hey, where are you? - Here I am!

note: A greeting between friends; colloquial variants «де си», «ђе си», often with «бре» or «брате».

examples.en: What are you doing in Belgrade?

examples.sr: Ооо, [о̀ткуд ти], нисмо се видели годинама!
examples.en: Oh, look who it is, we haven't seen each other in years!

note: Glad surprise at an unexpected meeting.

examples.en: How's it going? - Slowly but surely, getting by.
Nothing special, we're just plugging along.

note: In speech «гурати даље» means to cope, to get by as best you can.

meanings: to add fuel to the fire
forms: literally: to pour oil on the fire

examples.sr: Не [до̀ливај у̑ље на ва̏тру], причекај да се смири.
examples.en: Don't add fuel to the fire, wait for things to calm down.

examples.sr: Његови коментари само [до̀ливају у̑ље на ва̏тру].
examples.en: His comments only add fuel to the fire.

examples.sr: Имаш [гла̏дне о̏чи], напунио си тањир а ниси појео ништа.
examples.en: Your eyes are bigger than your stomach: you filled your plate and ate nothing.
He isn't hungry, his eyes are just bigger than his stomach.

meanings: to act as if one has just landed from another planet

examples.sr: Како не знаш за то? Јеси ли [па̑о с Ма̑рса]?
examples.en: How can you not know about that? Did you just land from Mars?

examples.sr: Понашаш се као да си [па̑о с Ма̑рса].
examples.en: You act as if you just landed from Mars.

forms: literally: there is no bread without a hoe

examples.sr: Ако хоћеш успех, ради: [не̏ма хле̏ба без мо̏тике].
examples.en: If you want success, work for it: no pain, no gain.
Study every day, no pain, no gain.

note: «мотика» is a hoe; colloquial «леба» for «хлеба» also occurs.

examples.sr: Код њега је живот [ме̑д и мле́ко].
examples.en: His life is all milk and honey.

examples.sr: Не очекуј да ће све бити [ме̑д и мле́ко].
examples.en: Don't expect everything to be smooth sailing.

meanings: be careful, don't do anything silly

examples.sr: Идете у град? Пазите се, [па̏ме̄т у гла̑ву]!
examples.en: Going into town? Take care, be sensible!
Going out tonight? Behave yourself!

note: A parting word from parents to children.

examples.sr: Цене у ресторанима на мору су [па̏прене].
examples.en: Prices in the seaside restaurants are sky-high.

examples.sr: За те [па̏прене це̏не] нећу ништа да купим.
examples.en: I won't buy anything at those crazy prices.

examples.sr: Нисам знао да су тротинети толико скупи. - Ма да, то је [ску̏по ка̏о о̀тров].
examples.en: I didn't know scooters were so expensive. - Yeah, they're insanely expensive.

examples.sr: Станови у центру су [ску̑пӣ ка̏о о̀тров].
examples.en: Apartments in the center are insanely expensive.

note: «као отров» intensifies any adjective in the sense of «terribly».

examples.en: A new car is just throwing money away.
Don't waste money on nonsense.

forms: literally: to cost like Saint Peter's scrambled eggs

examples.sr: Вечера овде [ко̏шта ка̏о Све̏тог Пе̏тра ка̏јгана].
examples.en: Dinner here costs a fortune.

examples.sr: Тај сат [ко̏шта ка̏о Све̏тог Пе̏тра ка̏јгана].
examples.en: That watch costs a fortune.

note: Colloquial hyperbole.

examples.sr: Таксиста нас је [о̏драо] за вожњу до аеродрома.
examples.en: The taxi driver ripped us off for the ride to the airport.
Don't go there, they'll fleece you.

note: In speech «одрао» is often shortened to «одро».

examples.en: Oh my goodness, what a crowd on the bus!
Good heavens, what have I done!

note: A mild substitute for a curse, expressing shock or surprise.

forms: literally: oh, all sorts of things

examples.sr: [Е̏, сва̏шта], то нисам очекивао од тебе.
examples.en: Well, I never, I didn't expect that from you.

examples.sr: Каже да је све било бесплатно? [Е̏, сва̏шта]!
examples.en: He says it was all free? Well, I never!

note: Reproach or disbelief; «свашта» on its own means «all sorts of things».

examples.en: Oh, all right, if that's what you say.
Well, fine, let's go then.
Where's the key? - I have no idea.
I have no idea what to do.

note: Colloquial; can be strengthened: «немам ни појма».

examples.sr: [Не сѐкирај се], стићи ћемо на време.
examples.en: Don't worry, we'll get there on time.
Just don't stress about it.

note: Close: «не брини», «немој да се оптерећујеш».

examples.en: Thanks, but there's no need.
There's no need to hurry.

note: A polite way to decline an offer; also «хвала, не треба».

examples.en: This meat is no good, it smells.
A habit like that is no good.

note: Colloquial; the opposite is «ваља» - fine, good.

examples.en: One round-trip ticket to Belgrade, please.
How much is a return ticket?

forms: literally: to give by the handful and by the capful

examples.sr: Он [да̏је ша̏ком и ка̏пом] добре оцене.
examples.en: He hands out good grades generously.

examples.sr: Ради за ту фирму и [де̏ли ша̏ком и ка̏пом].
examples.en: He works for that company and throws money around left and right.

note: Also «делити шаком и капом»; about generosity or extravagance.

examples.en: Only a handful of people came.

examples.sr: На сајму је био једва [ша̏чица] посетилаца.
examples.en: There were barely a handful of visitors at the fair.

meanings: to know like the back of one's hand
forms: literally: to hold in one's little finger

examples.sr: Он све правила [др̏жи у ма̏лом пр̏сту].
examples.en: He knows all the rules like the back of his hand.

examples.sr: Мој тата [др̏жи у ма̏лом пр̏сту] сваку улицу у граду.
examples.en: My dad knows every street in the city like the back of his hand.

meanings: to wrap someone around one's little finger
forms: literally: to spin someone around the little finger

examples.en: She has him wrapped around her little finger.

examples.sr: Не дај да те [вр̏те о̏ко ма̏лог пр̏ста].
examples.en: Don't let anyone wrap you around their little finger.

key: phr:не бити некоме ни за мали прст
meanings: can't hold a candle to someone
forms: literally: not to be even worth someone's little finger

examples.sr: Тај глумац јој [нѝје ни за ма̑ли пр̏ст].
examples.en: That actor can't hold a candle to her.

examples.sr: Данашњи глумци [ни́су ни за ма̑ли пр̏ст] старим мајсторима.
examples.en: Today's actors can't hold a candle to the old masters.

note: Stronger: «ни за црно испод нокта» - not worth even the dirt under a nail.

examples.en: He talks as if he knows everything.

examples.sr: Гледа ме [ка̏о да] сам му непријатељ.
examples.en: He looks at me as if I were his enemy.

note: Followed by present or past by meaning: «као да је јуче било» (as if it were yesterday).

key: phr:смејати се као луд на брашно
meanings: to laugh like a madman for no reason
forms: literally: to laugh like a madman at flour

examples.sr: Шта ти је? [Смѐје̄ш се ка̏о лу̑д на бра̏шно]!
examples.en: What's wrong with you? You're laughing like a madman!

examples.sr: Целу вечеру се [сме̏јао ка̏о лу̑д на бра̏шно].
examples.en: He laughed like a madman all evening.

note: Two origins are given: a Greek flour-sprinkling rite and a Macedonian prayer-over-flour cure.

forms: literally: to look through one's fingers

examples.sr: Инспектор је [про̀гледао кроз пр̏сте] њиховим прекршајима.
examples.en: The inspector turned a blind eye to their violations.

examples.sr: Не можемо више [про̀гледати кроз пр̏сте] том проблему.
examples.en: We can't turn a blind eye to this problem any longer.
They made the deal under the table.
The money was handed over on the sly.

note: About secret, illegal deals and payments.

examples.en: The gang laundered money through companies.
He is suspected of laundering money.
I got the tickets for free.

examples.sr: Није ништа купио, све је узео [за џа̏бе].
examples.en: He didn't buy anything, he got it all for free.

note: Colloquial, a Turkish loanword.

meanings: it does no harm to keep them

examples.en: Buy that too, it won't hurt.
Let them stay, they're not in the way.

note: Said of things you can keep in reserve: they get in nobody's way.

examples.en: He wants to do it at all costs.
The children wanted to go to the cinema at all costs.

note: Colloquial; close to «по сваку цену».

forms: literally: may his nice house be far away

examples.sr: Хоће да се жали? [Далѐко му ле̏па ку̏ћа]!
examples.en: He wants to complain? To hell with him!

examples.sr: Опет је касно дошао, [далѐко му ле̏па ку̏ћа].
examples.en: He came late again, good riddance to him.

note: Expresses contempt and not wanting to see the person; a bit rude.

meanings: um, what do you call it

examples.sr: Она је, [о̀ва̄ј, ка̏ко се зо̏ве], већ завршила то.
examples.en: She, um, what's her name, has already finished that.

examples.sr: Дошао је онај, [о̀ва̄ј, ка̏ко се зо̏ве], комшија.
examples.en: That, um, what's-his-name, the neighbor, came by.

note: A filler while you search for a name or a word.

examples.sr: [Ми̏слӣм], није лоше, али сам очекивао више.
examples.en: I mean, it's not bad, but I expected more.

examples.sr: Не знам шта да ти кажем, [ми̏слӣм], нисам упућен у ситуацију.
examples.en: I don't know what to tell you, I mean, I'm not up to speed on the situation.

note: A colloquial marker; similar are «оно» and «значи».

examples.sr: Кафа је на мом рачуну, [ку̏ћа ча̏сти]!
examples.en: The coffee is on us - on the house!
Dessert is on the house.
Put your wallet away, it's my treat.
Tonight I'm buying for everyone.

note: A variant: «на мој рачун» - on me.

examples.en: Please, help yourself to the cakes.
Help yourself, no need to ask.

note: A variant: «узмите слободно» - take some, don't be shy.

examples.en: I can't wait to see you!
The kids can't wait for the vacation.

note: Literally «I barely wait», but the sense is positive: eager anticipation.

examples.en: So much work, and all for nothing.

examples.sr: Оставили су нас без одговора, [џа̏бе смо кре̏чили].
examples.en: They left us without an answer, we did it all for nothing.

note: An ironic remark when effort brought no result; also «џабе сам кречио», «џабе смо кречили».

examples.en: He won the lottery? No way!

examples.sr: [Ма̏ да̑ј], то не може бити истина.
examples.en: Come on, that can't be true.

note: A reaction to unexpected news; on its own «дај» is just «give».

forms: literally: that's how that is for you

examples.en: It didn't work out, that's how it goes.

examples.sr: Не секирај се, [та̀ко̄ ти је то̑] у животу.
examples.en: Don't worry, that's life.

note: A calm, philosophical tone: accepting the situation.

meanings: oh, come on, don't make a drama of it
forms: literally: let go of that story

examples.en: Oh, come on, it's not that bad.

examples.sr: [Ма̏ пу̑стӣ при̏чу] и дођи на кафу.
examples.en: Oh, drop it and come over for a coffee.

note: A friendly way to calm someone who is exaggerating.

examples.sr: Рекао сам ти да ће касни. [Е̏то ти]!
examples.en: I told you he'd be late. See!
There you go, it's started raining.

note: A short, convincing remark when the outcome is obvious.

examples.en: She left him? Wow!
Wow, I can't believe it!

note: A reaction to striking news or gossip, often not negative.

examples.sr: Кад устанем, [вр̏ти ми се у гла̏ви].
examples.en: When I stand up, I feel dizzy.

examples.sr: Од вожње [вр̏ти ми се у гла̏ви].
examples.en: Traveling makes me dizzy.
The noise makes my head split.
My head is splitting, I need a pill.
I feel sick, I have to sit down.
I'm sick of his stories.

note: «мука ми је од чега» - to be sick of something.

examples.sr: Учио сам два месеца, положићу [јѐдан кроз јѐдан].
examples.en: I studied for two months, I'll pass for sure.
The victory will be a sure thing.

note: Colloquial: a hundred percent, no two ways about it.

examples.sr: Стигли смо на станицу [у пе̑т до два́нае̄ст].
examples.en: We got to the station at the last minute.

examples.sr: Он увек све ради [у пе̑т до два́нае̄ст].
examples.en: He always does everything at the last minute.
The wind was blowing at full blast.

examples.sr: Радили су [све̏ у шѐснае̄ст] да заврше посао.
examples.en: They worked flat out to finish the job.

examples.sr: [Ни пе̑т ни ше̑ст], одмах јој је пришао.
examples.en: Without a second thought, he went straight up to her.

examples.sr: Одлучио је [ни пе̑т ни ше̑ст] да се исели.
examples.en: He decided on the spot to move out.

examples.sr: Закаснио си? [Ма̏ не̏ма вѐзе], стигли смо на време.
examples.en: You're late? Never mind, we made it on time.

examples.sr: [Ма̏ не̏ма вѐзе], нека буде како хоћеш.
examples.en: It doesn't matter, let it be as you like.

note: «нема везе» alone: never mind, it doesn't matter.

meanings: thanks for the offer, but (a polite refusal)

examples.sr: [Хва́ла на по̀нуди, а̏ли] тренутно нисам заинтересован.
examples.en: Thanks for the offer, but I'm not interested right now.

examples.sr: [Хва́ла на по̀нуди, а̏ли] мислим да ћу изабрати нешто друго.
examples.en: Thanks for the offer, but I think I'll choose something else.

key: phr:жао ми је, али имам друге планове
meanings: I'm sorry, but I have other plans

examples.sr: [Жа̏о ми је, а̏ли ѝма̄м дру̑ге пла̏нове].
examples.en: I'm sorry, but I have other plans.

examples.sr: Позив је диван, [жа̏о ми је, а̏ли ѝма̄м дру̑ге пла̏нове].
examples.en: It's a lovely invitation, I'm sorry, but I have other plans.

forms: literally: it is not the right moment

examples.en: I appreciate the offer, but it's not the right moment.

examples.sr: Знам да желиш да причамо, али [нѝје пра̑вӣ трену́так].
examples.en: I know you want to talk, but it's not the right time.
Unfortunately, I can't come tonight.
Thanks, but unfortunately I can't.

note: The most universal polite refusal.

examples.sr: [Чи̏ни ми се да] имамо довољно времена.
examples.en: It seems to me that we have enough time.
It seems to me it's going to rain.

note: Less categorical than «мислим да».

examples.en: As far as I know, the meeting is tomorrow.

examples.sr: [Колѝко ја̏ зна̑м], он је у Нишу.
examples.en: As far as I know, he's in Niš.

examples.sr: [Мо̀жда гре̏шим, а̏ли] мислим да је ово тачно.
examples.en: I may be wrong, but I think this is correct.

examples.sr: [Мо̀жда гре̏шим, а̏ли] он је већ отишао.
examples.en: I may be wrong, but he has already left.
You're right, that's important.
I think he's right.

note: «бити у праву» - to be right; the negative is «нисам у праву».

examples.sr: [Не сла̏жем се у по̏тпуности] са твојим мишљењем.
examples.en: I don't fully agree with your opinion.

examples.sr: [Не сла̏жем се у по̏тпуности], али разумем те.
examples.en: I don't fully agree, but I understand you.

key: phr:пу, пу да те не урекнем
meanings: touch wood, so I don't jinx you (said of a baby)

examples.sr: Јао, како си велики! [Пу̏, пу̏ да те не у̀рекнем]!
examples.en: Oh, how big you are! Touch wood, so I don't jinx you!

note: Said to avert the evil eye, with a light pretend spit.

examples.en: I lived in Kaliningrad for a whole month.
He studied guitar for exactly a year.

note: Likewise «годину дана», «недељу дана»; «за недељу дана» - in a week.

examples.en: I waited for you for a whole hour.
I've been working here for an hour.

note: «сат» + a fixed «времена»; stresses exactly one hour.

examples.en: You have to take care of your health.

note: Usually with «о» + loc.: «о здрављу», «о времену».

examples.sr: Током путовања почела је да [во̀ди дне̑внӣк].
examples.en: During the trip she started keeping a diary.
Her family originates from Russia.

note: Bookish; «порекло» means origin.

meanings: to do most of the talking
to take the lead in a conversation

examples.sr: На састанку је [во̀дио гла̏вну ре̑ч] он.
examples.en: He dominated the conversation at the meeting.
The company keeps records of working hours.

meanings: as many sparks, as much health (a Christmas blessing)

examples.sr: [Колѝко ва̏рница, толѝко̄ здра̑вља], среће и весеља!
examples.en: As many sparks, as much health, happiness and joy!

note: Said by the «положајник», the first Christmas visitor, as he stirs the fire with a twig of the Yule log.

key: phr:учини добро, не кај се; учини зло, надај се
meanings: do good and don't regret it; do evil and expect payback
forms: literally: do good - don't repent; do evil - expect (punishment)

examples.sr: Не жали, [у̏чини до̀бро, не ка̏ј се; у̏чини зло̏, на̏дај се].
examples.en: Don't regret helping: do good and don't repent, do evil and expect payback.

note: A consolation for someone who helped people and got no thanks; «надај се» here means «expect payback».

key: phr:новци кад одлазе имају сто ногу, а кад долазе само две
meanings: money goes fast and comes slowly
forms: literally: money, when it leaves, has a hundred legs, and when it comes, only two

examples.sr: Годину дана смо штедели, а за недељу дана све потрошили: [но̑вци ка̏д о̀длазе и̏мају сто̑ но̏гу, а ка̏д до̀лазе са̏мо две̑].
examples.en: We saved for a year and spent it all in a week: money has a hundred legs when it leaves and only two when it comes.

note: «новци» is a dialectal form of «новац».

key: phr:роди ме, мајко, срећног, па ме на ђубре баци
forms: literally: bear me lucky, mother, and then throw me on the dump

examples.sr: Он је лењ, а има све: [ро̏ди ме, ма̏јко, сре̏ћног, па ме на ђу̏бре ба̏ци].
examples.en: He's lazy and yet has everything: bear me lucky, mother, then throw me on the dump.

note: Said about someone else's luck; variant: «Роди ме, мајко, без главе, само немој без среће».

examples.en: Let's not discuss it now, later, later.

note: Colloquial: a way to put off a talk or a task.

examples.sr: То ће бити готово [Бо̑г зна̏ ка̏д].
examples.en: It'll be ready God knows when.
Someday you'll understand it.

meanings: in the blink of an eye

examples.en: I'll finish this in the blink of an eye.
The repair is a quick job.

note: Literally «an hour of work»; means quick and easy.

examples.en: We'll have coffee at a leisurely pace.

note: Of Turkish origin; colloquial.

examples.en: Don't plan too much, whatever will be, will be.
No rush, we can do it later.

note: «фрка» means fuss or haste; colloquial, youth slang.

examples.en: Sooner or later you'll have to decide.
Should I lend you some money? Not a chance!

note: An ironic refusal; colloquial.

examples.en: Do you want to go? - No way!

note: «јок» is Turkish for «no»; colloquial, a flat refusal.

meanings: to have a knack for something

examples.en: He has a knack for repairs.

note: «кликер» is a glass marble; colloquial.

meanings: I like it when we're together

examples.sr: [При̏ја ми ка̏д смо за̏једно] у тишини.
examples.en: I like being together in silence.

note: «прија ми» - it feels good to me, I like it.

examples.sr: Било је лепо, [са то̏бо̄м је вре́ме про̀летело].
examples.en: It was lovely, time flew by with you.

meanings: something is going on between us

examples.sr: Осећам да се [не̏што дѐшава и̏змеђу нас].
examples.en: I feel that something is going on between us.

meanings: we have to do this again

examples.en: That was great, we have to do this again!

examples.sr: Услови рада у тој фирми су [у на̏јмању ру̏ку] понижавајући.
examples.en: Working conditions at that company are humiliating, to say the least.

note: Bookish, often used when judging something.

examples.sr: Плата је лоша, али [а̏ко ни̏шта дру̏го], иде ти стаж.
examples.en: The pay is bad, but if nothing else, it counts toward your work record.

examples.sr: Дошао сам [чи̏сто да] видим да ли сте добро.
examples.en: I came just to check that you're all right.

examples.sr: Учим мало јапански, [те̏к да] могу да се споразумем у продавници.
examples.en: I'm studying a little Japanese, just enough to get by in a store.

examples.sr: Учио је [те̏к толѝко̄ да] положи испит.
examples.en: He studied just enough to pass the exam.

meanings: thanks, I don't need a bag

examples.en: Thanks, I don't need a bag, I have my own.
I have small change, don't worry.

note: What you tell a cashier to avoid trouble with change.

forms: literally: can you make it small

examples.en: Can you break this banknote?

note: «уситнити» literally means to make small: this is how you ask for change.

meanings: to have butterflies in one's stomach

examples.sr: Кад га види, одмах [и̏ма лѐптириће у сто̏маку].
examples.en: Whenever she sees him, she gets butterflies in her stomach right away.

examples.sr: Шта је било, [ма̏чка ти је по̀јела јѐзик]?
examples.en: What's the matter, cat got your tongue?

note: Said to someone who suddenly went quiet.

forms: literally: to mix old women and frogs

examples.sr: Не можеш то поредити, [ме̏шаш ба́бе̄ и жа̏бе]!
examples.en: You can't compare those, you're mixing apples and oranges!

meanings: I can barely keep my eyes open

examples.en: It's late, my eyes are closing.
After lunch my eyelids are heavy.
Since this morning I've been dead on my feet.
After the move I was dog-tired.

examples.sr: Дај ми кафу, [мо̏зак ми не ра̏ди].
examples.en: Give me a coffee, my brain isn't working.
Tonight I was dying of exhaustion.

note: «цркнути» is rude and normally said of animals; used jokingly of people.

meanings: it's all the same to me

examples.en: - Tea or coffee? - I don't mind.

examples.sr: Не желим да чујем, [ба̏ш ме бри̏га]!
examples.en: I don't want to hear it, I couldn't care less!

note: A bit rude; shows irritation.

examples.en: - When should we come? - I don't mind.

note: A word of Hungarian origin, used in Vojvodina even by people who don't speak Hungarian.

key: phr:све му је равно до косова
forms: literally: to him everything is flat all the way to Kosovo

examples.sr: Пропустио је рок, а [све̏ му је ра̑вно до Ко̏сова].
examples.en: He missed the deadline and doesn't care about anything.

note: Joking, of an indifferent person; such people supposedly live a hundred years.

key: phr:зато што сам ја тако рекла

examples.sr: - Зашто? - [За̀то̄ што̏ сам ја̏ та̀ко̄ ре̏кла]!
examples.en: - Why? - Because I said so!

note: A classic parental line; a man says «рекао».

key: phr:видећеш кад ти отац дође кући
meanings: just wait till your father gets home

examples.en: Just wait till your father gets home!

note: A parental threat.

examples.en: Whose are you, my child? What family are you from?

note: Serbs like to ask about family and roots: this asks which family you come from.

examples.en: Everything is ready, let's go!

note: From the film «Ко то тамо пева»; a call to get started.

examples.sr: Џабе се смеје, [Ла̏кӣ је ма̏ло не̏рво̄зан].
examples.en: He's laughing for nothing, Laki is a little nervous.

note: A quote from the film «Маратонци трче почасни круг»; said when someone is furious.

examples.en: Again right at the end: less wine!

note: A quote from the film «Лажно лето 68».

key: phr:никада они не могу мене толико мало да плате колико ја могу мало да радим
meanings: however little they pay me, I can work even less

examples.sr: Знаш како кажу: [ни̏када о̏ни не мо̀гу ме̏не толѝко̄ ма̏ло да пла̏те колѝко ја̏ мо̀гу ма̏ло да ра̏дим].
examples.en: You know what they say: they can never pay me so little that I can't work even less.

note: A line from the film «Јагоде у грлу», a symbol of an attitude to work.

examples.en: Happy birthday! All the best!

note: Birthdays are usually marked by singing «Данас нам је диван дан».

examples.en: We want to surprise him.
It's urgent? Yeah, I'm running as we speak!

note: A sarcastic reply to a demand for «urgent».

examples.sr: Од данас, [за̏боље ме]! Радите шта хоћете.
examples.en: From today on, I couldn't care less! Do what you want.

note: A mild colloquial form instead of ruder variants.

examples.en: The family has preserved the tradition for centuries.

key: phr:село гори, а баба се чешља
forms: literally: the village is on fire and the old woman is combing her hair

examples.sr: Сви причају о несрећи, а она о плановима за викенд: [се̏ло го̏ри, а ба̏ба се че̏шља].
examples.en: Everyone is talking about the disaster, and she about her weekend plans: fiddling while Rome burns.

note: Of someone busy with trifles when an urgent problem needs solving; also the name of a Serbian TV series.
